source.title: FairSteer: Inference Time Debiasing for LLMs with Dynamic Activation Steering
source.authors: Yichen Li; Zhi-Ting Fan; Rui-Zhe Chen; Xiaotang Gai; Lu-Qi Gong; Yan Zhang; Zuo-Zhu Liu

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses the linear representation hypothesis to motivate an inference-time debiasing method, but does not test superposition, feature-capacity competition, or any of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports measurements of linear separability and geometry for fairness-related activations; these are recorded as findings about a related construct under fits_no_version. Its QA, generation, and capability results evaluate FairSteer’s debiasing performance, not the claim’s predicted behavior, and are not rows. Layer-selection accuracy is used to choose a layer and is not recorded as a result row.
record.test_reason: FairSteer cites Toy Models of Superposition only as background for the linear representation hypothesis. Its own measurements are linear-probe accuracy on biased vs unbiased answer labels, a PCA plot, and cosine similarity between steering vectors. None measures features outnumbering dimensions, polysemantic neurons, capacity competition, SAE recovery, or feature dimensionality. The remaining results report how well the authors' debiasing method performs.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that fairness-related features are encoded in linearly separable directions, and that FairSteer reduces bias across question-answering, counterfactual and generation tasks while largely preserving capability. They draw no conclusions about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses linear classifiers to detect bias signatures and adds contrastive mean-difference steering vectors during inference. It does not use or reproduce the toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Classifier accuracy varies across layers and social-group categories; category-specific classifiers generalize less well to other categories. The paper also reports that intervention strength affects accuracy and bias scores, but these intervention results do not test the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes separate biased from unbiased answer-state activations: above 90% at intermediate layers and above 87% at the final layer, across six LLMs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fairness-related answer states are linearly decodable from LLM residual activations, peaking at intermediate layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering vectors computed per social category have pairwise cosine similarity above 0.90 in Llama2-13B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Debiasing directions are largely shared across social-group categories.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The paper provides no uncertainty estimates for the relevant activation-separability or DSV-similarity findings. The geometric visualization is a 2-D PCA projection, and the linear-classifier evidence concerns the paper’s biased/unbiased labels rather than superposition. The authors also note limitations in the prompt-pair representativeness and generalizability beyond the six open-source models tested.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted FairSteer debiasing outcomes on BBQ, UNQOVER, CrowS-Pairs, CEB, and capability benchmarks because they assess the proposed method’s performance rather than the claim’s predicted representation behavior. Also omitted layer-selection accuracies used to select the intervention layer. These results appear in Sections 4.1–4.6 and Tables 1–3.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, interference or geometry of superposed features.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity allocation.
No analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.
No neuron-spread or SAE/dictionary analysis in LLMs.
Uses a single mean-difference direction, but never tests 1-D against multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche T4 is confirmed. The citation of the original source is background motivation only. All rows are related-construct findings, not tests of any version.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, sparse feature capacity, overlapping representations, interference, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry are tested.
No polysemantic neurons, capacity competition, or allocation of dedicated versus shared dimensions are tested.
The study does not investigate alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity indicates superposition.
No neuron-level feature spreading or SAE/dictionary recovery in LLMs is measured.
No SAE features or their completeness, stability, or canonical status are studied.
The paper uses mean-difference steering vectors, but does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional, or whether features are superposed.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B
rows.operation_detail: Trained layer-wise linear classifiers to distinguish biased from unbiased activations; reported validation accuracy.

conditions.value: biased and unbiased activation validation set

rows.note: This measures separability of the paper’s fairness-related labels, not feature overlap, capacity pressure, or superposition.
rows.check: Probe separability of the model's answer labels (biased vs unbiased); not a superposition measure. The subject is Mistral-7B v0.3-instruct.

rows.subject: all six tested LLMs
rows.operation_detail: Trained layer-wise linear classifiers to distinguish biased from unbiased activations; reported final-layer validation accuracy across models.

conditions.value: Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B, Llama3-8B, Vicuna-7B, Vicuna-13B, Mistral-7B

rows.note: Aggregate statement across the six listed models; this does not test any listed superposition version.
rows.check: Aggregate statement across six models; same construct as R1.

rows.subject: Vicuna-13B
rows.operation_detail: Projected layer-14 biased and unbiased activations into two dimensions using PCA and displayed their mean difference.
rows.measure: Visual separation of biased and unbiased activation clusters
rows.value: The text describes a clear separation between clusters; the mean-difference arrow is described as the DSV.
rows.note: A visualization of biased/unbiased activation labels, not a test of overlapping feature directions or dimensionality of superposed features.
rows.check: Qualitative 2-D PCA visualization with no number; it cannot show superposition.

rows.subject: Llama2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Trained category-specific linear classifiers and evaluated them on category validation sets.
rows.value: greater than 90% on its own category’s validation set
rows.note: The paper reports the category-generalization comparison in aggregate.
rows.check: Category-specific probe accuracy; a related construct only.

rows.subject: Llama2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated each category-specific linear classifier on validation sets from other categories.
rows.value: below 80% on validation sets from other categories
rows.note: This is the contrast to the same-category result in R4; the paper uses it to discuss category-specific classifier performance.
rows.check: Cross-category probe accuracy (below 80). Not a test of any version.

rows.subject: Llama2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Compared category-specific debiasing steering vectors using pairwise cosine similarity.

conditions.value: DSVs for different BBQ social-group categories

rows.measure: Pairwise cosine similarity between category DSVs
rows.note: Similarity among steering vectors does not establish feature overlap or that the features are one-dimensional.
rows.check: Cosine similarity between steering vectors; this does not test the dimensionality of superposed features.

rows.subject: Llama2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Compared the DSV computed from all categories with each category-specific DSV using cosine similarity.

conditions.value: all-category DSV versus each category DSV

rows.value: greater than 0.95 for comparisons with any other category’s DSV
rows.note: This is a reported similarity result for the paper’s steering vectors, not a test of the listed superposition versions.
